_README: The ISL pin this repo's PLoT -> ISL request drift pairing is derived against.
Contract step-2 slice 2. Hand-edited ONLY when deliberately re-pinning ISL.
RE-PINNING PROCEDURE (all four steps, in order — the standing test fails if
any is skipped, which is the point):
1. Fresh blobless clone of the ISL repo at the new sha, OUTSIDE this repo.
asserts that the committed replay transcript was generated against exactly
this pin (transcript.pin_digest == sha256 of the canonical form of this file).
Bumping the pin without re-running the driver therefore turns the suite RED
instead of leaving a pairing silently derived against stale bytes.

isl.pinned_by: R1 S3 deliberate re-pin, 2026-09-28 (R3 SCIENCE, #72 5875939395): 686fcb7 -> 56c35468, the served ISL R1 S2 build (ISL #205; SERVED, AIQ #72 5875792434). It declares GoalConstraint.value_frame / goal_threshold_frame change_abs | change_rel, NodeV2.quantity_frame and NodeV2.raw_range, which this PR's egress sends; the 686fcb7 pin predates all four, so the pairing would have read them as undeclared. runtime.why_these: src/config/__init__.py imports pydantic_settings as a package-init side effect, and src/utils/correlation.py imports numpy at module scope. Both are hard requirements of merely IMPORTING RobustnessRequestV2 — neither is obvious from the model file.

isl_openapi_json.what_it_is: ISL's committed, MACHINE-GENERATED OpenAPI document (scripts/generate_openapi.py -> FastAPI app.openapi()). It is Pydantic's own description of the mounted request models, not a hand-written copy — which is why the pairing may consume it hermetically. ISL CI (.github/workflows/openapi-validation.yml) runs `generate_openapi.py --check` on every PR touching src/api, src/models, pyproject or the spec, so it cannot drift from the models without ISL going red.
isl_openapi_json.what_it_is_NOT: It is not evidence about DEPLOYED ISL. It describes the app as built at this sha.

source_sha256._note: The model + router files every claim in the pairing is derived from. The Python replay driver verifies each of these against the clone it is pointed at and REFUSES to run on a mismatch, so a transcript can never be produced from bytes other than these.
